title: Mattiah ben Shmuel
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He appears at the beginning of Mishnah Shekalim, chapter 5, as Mattehiah ben Shmuel, one of the Temple’s fifteen officials, in charge of the lotteries. The Mishnah of the Westerners reads Mattiyeh ben Shmuel.

Tamid 3:2 has Mattiya ben Shmuel saying, “The whole eastern horizon has lit up.” This implies that he disagrees with the first, anonymous Tanna; alternatively, the Mishnah is recounting what Mattiya ben Shmuel used to say.

And in Yoma, beginning of chapter 3, the name there is Mattehiya; in Tamid, chapter 3, mishnah 2, the name there is Mattiah; and in the Mishnah of the Westerners, Mattiyeh. Hyman infers from this that these were all names of a single sage who lived in the time of the Temple.

notes.text: The alternative explanation is Hyman’s: this may be an actual disagreement or a description of the official’s customary words. The five spellings of Mattiah’s name are retained rather than harmonized.

The consulted Mishnah Tamid 3:2 directly has Matya ben Shmuel and the illuminated eastern horizon. The supplied name spellings, Temple-period identity inference and the alternative between disagreement and customary official speech remain Hyman’s; the exact Mishnah of the Westerners reading was not inspected here.
